title: geckolib issue #767: Mod causes resource loading errors for non-geckolib animation files

text:
[issue by DarksideAlex]

**Versions**:
- Minecraft: 1.20.1
- Quilt: 0.29.1
- GeckoLib: 4.8

[comment by Tslat (collaborator)]
What mod is using the animations folder?

mcinspects isn't even on 1.20.1 is it?

[comment by DarksideAlex (none)]
Private fork of MCInspects with 1.20.1 support and data--driven animations. That shouldn’t matter though, since mcinspects only adds a json file under its own namespace and doesn’t use geckolib. The issue is that geckolib tries to load it anyway and cancels resource loading that way.

[comment by Tslat (collaborator)]
Geckolib tries to load it in anyway because it uses the `animations` folder, and has for a very long time

If you're forking a newer mod, change the directory it uses so it doesn't clash with GeckoLib
In future versions, GeckoLib has its own directory it uses so that this doesn't happen, but in 1.20.1 if you make a mod that conflicts with an existing mod, it's your job to fix the conflict, not mine

[comment by DarksideAlex (none)]
Why not add a simple try...catch though? That's basically all I'm asking. Also, why should it be my job to fix the conflict? After all, it's geckolib accessing files in a generically-named folder under a rather distinct namespace unrelated to geckolib and causing a crash while doing so.

[comment by Tslat (collaborator)]
It's not a distinct namespace

Assets load from all namespaces, that's how assets work.
It's _your_ job because you're the one adding assets to a folder that GeckoLib was already using as its standard, and has been for a very long time, and is pretty well established.

[comment by Tslat (collaborator)]
> Yep, this is the exact same issue, caused by honestly bad code. I really don't get how Tslat still won't admit that a mod crashing the game is bad, no matter "who came first"

I agree
A mod crashing the game is bad, no matter who came first.

This is also why this problem was fixed entirely in newer versions, where I stopped relying on a generic folder for these things.
The _problem_ is that I can't be made responsible for every other mod suddenly jamming things into a place GeckoLib has been using for a long time.
It's a game of whack-a-mole that never ends, and somehow it's GeckoLib's responsibility to fix collisions that other mods created?

GeckoLib _already_ manually patches out certain namespaces to avoid this, because this has come up in the past, so clearly it's not something I can just keep adding namespaces to, because it never ends.
Which is why I leave it to the developer of the _newer_ mod to reverse the collision, since newer usually means less established footprint, so a lower impact of having to make a breaking change.

For me to move the animations folder _now_ would be catastrophic

Either way I'll probably just change this to spamming the log with errors instead of outright breaking since obviously crashing is the lesser goal here, but I'm not sure why I'm the one copping flak over something that a newly created mod is causing. Why is it not on them?
